name: Quess Corp Ltd
title: Quess Corp Ltd - 539978 - Transcript Of Earnings Call - Q2 FY27

read.thesis: Quess Q2 FY27 revenue +15% YoY with ~21k GS net adds, but Professional Staffing margin slid to 10.5% on front-loaded IT investment; management still guides PS margin 11-12% for FY27 and exit near 12%.

summary.headline: Quess Q2 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR4,396 crores, with PAT up 44% to INR75 crores, helped by a INR120 crore one-time Labour Code pass-through.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY and 5% QoQ to INR4,396 crores, with adjusted EBITDA up 20% YoY to INR92 crores at a 2.1% margin. Reported PAT rose 44% YoY to INR75 crores, though it fell sequentially because Q1 included INR24 crores of one-time tax-refund other income. Headcount rose by a net 20,857 in General Staffing, and management said the add was concentrated in September. Professional Staffing margins fell to 10.5% on front-loaded IT Solutions investment, while management said gross margin in that segment grew 12% YoY.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (excl. non-cash ESOP INR6 crores)

segments.name: General Staffing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,823 crores, +15% YoY (about +12% excluding INR120 crore Labour Code impact); EBITDA INR57 crores, +23% YoY. Net add 20,857 associates, 116 new contracts, record collections of INR4,285 crores, DSO 24 days.

segments.name: Professional Staffing (Quess IT Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR254 crores, +13% YoY; EBITDA INR27 crores, down 2% YoY, margin 10.5% vs 12.2% a year ago. 27 new contracts in Q2 (62 in H1); headcount 7,566 after net add of 437. Gross margin 20.5% vs 17.5% two years ago.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Revenue INR318 crores, +10% YoY, -4% QoQ; EBITDA INR22 crores, +23% YoY, margin 6.9% vs 6.2% in Q1. Malaysia revenue +50% YoY, Philippines +15%; Middle East flat with 14.2% margin. 33 new contracts.

segments.name: Digital platform (BCPL)
segments.commentary: Turned EBITDA positive in Q2 after burn of nearly INR6 crores in FY26; paying clients rose from 14 in March to 54 in September. Management expects full-year FY27 breakeven.

guidance_outlook: General Staffing net additions guided at 10,000 to 15,000 per quarter as steady state; management said it may exceed this, and that things looked decent as of end-October.
Professional Staffing margin guidance of 11% to 12% for FY27, with exit near 12%; management said margin would have been 11.7% excluding the investment.
Labour Code one-time revenue: management sees no material residual impact in H2 FY27 (about 95-96% compliant at H1, 96.5% of payrolls done per Q&A).
Unallocated corporate cost (ESOP-related) expected at about INR20 crores in FY27, tapering to about INR15 crores in year 2.
Interim dividend of INR5 per share approved.
AI query system QMS targets answering half of associate queries by December 2026 and up to 80% by March 2027; Brain channel expects 35,000 to 40,000 offers in H2.
capex_capacity: Quess IT Solutions investment is strategic and multi-year (3 to 4 years), covering leadership, sales, delivery and practices; management compared it to FY21-22 investment that lifted EBITDA from INR31 crores to about INR110 crores run-rate.
Project Confluence (client sale to payroll, collections on one platform): Phase 1 goes live in January 2027, further phases in 2027.
Fractional workforce platform: first deal with a large FMCG brand for about 350 associates; full digital platform live by January 2027.
Open mandates in General Staffing stable at 30,000 to 35,000.
Global corridors: 135 workers mobilised to UAE in H1; MOU with IOM signed.
demand_pricing: Headcount about 504,000, +4% YoY and +5% QoQ; manufacturing added 7,800 associates in the quarter, with about 10 car makers as customers.
Gross margin in General Staffing and Professional Staffing both rose; PS gross margin grew 12% YoY, 3% QoQ.
PAPM steady at INR650 to 700; construction, VAS and manufacturing together are about 20% of mix, and higher-margin businesses are expected to lift PAPM over time.
Top-10 customers in Professional Staffing rose from 40% to 46% of revenue, with 62 new MSAs added in H1.
Management said the 80JJAA tax matter has four favourable precedents; hearing deferred from October to January.

qa_highlights.question: Why did General Staffing headcount add of 20,000 translate into only about 12% revenue growth excluding Labour Code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adds came late in the quarter, with about 65% in September and less than 33% in July-August, so revenue lags into Q3. It cited 116 new contracts and Brain sourcing as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mix shift to CRT and manufacturing sustain volume growth, and what does it mean for margins and collect-and-pay?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher-margin businesses (construction, VAS, manufacturing) are about 18-20% of mix; traditional flat-fee businesses are 80-82%. Collect-and-pay moved about 1% lower, which management attributed to customer mix; DSO was stable at 24 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Professional Staffing margin fall and what is steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment in IT Solutions drove the margin decline; ex-investment PS margin would have been 11.7%. FY27 guidance is 11-12%, exit near 12%. Top-10 share rose to 46%, and MSP declined due to one particular account.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the INR8 crore rise in unallocated corporate cost, and what is the trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to front-loaded non-cash ESOP accounting. FY27 expected at about INR20 crores, tapering to about INR15 crores in year 2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Labour Code residual impact and the EPF wage-ceiling effect?
qa_highlights.answer: No material residual H2 impact expected. The wage ceiling change from INR15,000 to INR25,000 raises employee contributions to about INR3,000 per month and slightly lifts revenue; management said 96.5% of payrolls were completed.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled receivables and old receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR300 crores of unbilled is from Labour Code provisions and will remain unbilled until employees are paid; the rest reflects 15% growth. The INR11 crore over-3-year item relates to ECL on unbilled revenue.

risks_watch: Revenue lag from late-quarter headcount adds; Q3 General Staffing revenue must show the flow-through.
Professional Staffing EBITDA margin at 10.5%, below the 12.2% year-ago level; recovery to 11-12% guidance is needed.
Pending EPFO demand of INR72 crores (no hearing date) and 80JJAA tax matter (hearing moved to January 2027).
Non-top-10 Professional Staffing customer revenue moderating; top-10 concentration at 46%.
Collect-and-pay share and higher-credit customer mix (15-30 day credit) could pressure working capital.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and cash collection, with specific numbers and milestone timelines. Cautious and deflecting on Professional Staffing margin, the mix shift in General Staffing and the EPFO and 80JJAA matters, where answers defaulted to hearings and precedents.
key_quotes: Our cash collection in this quarter was the highest ever, crossing INR5,000 crores.
Today, the contribution from the second half of this segment of the higher-margin businesses is nearly 18% to 20%, but the traditional businesses still continue to contribute around 80% to 82%.
An investment of this magnitude is not for the current financial year only. It is for the next 3 to 4 financial years.

growth.why: Q2 revenue rose 15% YoY (about 12% excluding the one-time Labour Code pass-through) and management guides General Staffing net adds of 10,000-15,000 per quarter and PS margin of 11-12% for FY27, backed by headcount wins, 116 GS contracts and a 27-contract PS pipeline, but no explicit revenue growth guide or capacity additions were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: PS margin at 10.5% in Q2 vs 11-12% FY27 guide with exit near 12% (11.7% ex-investment), and BCPL turned EBITDA positive with FY27 breakeven expected; adjusted EBITDA margin 2.1% in Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants or sites named, but Project Confluence Phase 1 goes live January 2027 and fractional workforce platform live January 2027; these are platforms rather than physical capacity, and open mandates stable at 30,000-35,000.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: General Staffing net adds guided at 10,000-15,000 per quarter with headcount ~504,000 (+4% YoY), 20,857 net add in Q2 with ~65% in September so revenue flows into Q3; Brain channel expects 35,000-40,000 offers in H2.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said General Staffing adds may exceed 10,000-15,000 per quarter and things looked decent at end-October, but no explicit revenue guide raise was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 General Staffing revenue must show flow-through from late-quarter adds; PS margin at 10.5% against 11-12% FY27 guide requires recovery, and EPFO INR72 crore demand and 80JJAA hearing are pending.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Project Confluence Phase 1 (client sale to payroll and collections on one platform) and fractional workforce digital platform both go live January 2027, with further Confluence phases in 2027.

rows.label: Fractional workforce platform first FMCG deal
rows.why: First deal with a large FMCG brand for about 350 associates is already signed, with full digital platform live by January 2027.

rows.label: BCPL digital platform FY27 breakeven
rows.why: Turned EBITDA positive in Q2 after nearly INR6 crore burn in FY26; paying clients rose from 14 to 54 between March and September, and management expects full-year FY27 breakeven.

rows.label: AI query system QMS deflection
rows.why: Targets answering half of associate queries by December 2026 and up to 80% by March 2027, aimed at cost efficiency in General Staffing.

tone.note: Management was confident on headcount adds, record collections above INR5,000 crore and milestone timelines, but cautious and deflecting on the Professional Staffing margin, General Staffing mix shift and the EPFO and 80JJAA matters; analysts pressed on revenue lag from late-quarter adds and PS marg
